newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on
Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Sri Lanka to revamp public administration in line with former Ceylon Civil Service, as part of public sector reforms programme, which are designed to boost efficiency, says Public Administration and Home Affairs Minister, Ratnasiri Wickremanayake.

Douglas Devananda, leader of the Tamil political party Eelam People's Democratic Party (EPDP), says his party which was the first to return to the northern Jaffna area, will expand activities to the entire peninsula.
Police detain an Army vehicle with nearly three million rupees worth of illegally felled timber in Hingurakkgoda, in central Sri Lanka.
Education Ministry to use lottery scheme to choose students for entry to year one in popular schools, in a bid to eradicate malpractices associated with the current selection process.
Government to introduce new pension scheme for university employees.
EPDP's Douglas Devananda says he will act to bring normalcy in north, since Jaffna people feel current peace is temporary.
Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte says TNL, a private television network, has broadcast scandalous news in last few months.
Main opposition United National Party member Jayalath Jayawardena says UNP will act in responsible manner to solve national crisis.
